name: Sorghastrum

priority: lemma awn bend count and length
study_strategy.warning: Do not treat statewide Texas nativity as local presence. S. elliottii is much more eastern in Texas.
look_here_first_sequence: 1. Confirm Poaceae from culm node, sheath and ligule; inspect a mature collar, not just a yellow plume.
2. Confirm Sorghastrum from a branched panicle with awned fertile spikelets accompanied by reduced hairy sterile pedicels; inspect one branch joint.
3. Compare panicle density/hairs and count the bends of several complete lemma awns with a millimeter ruler.
4. Check basal growth for short scaly rhizomes, culm-node hairs and matched leaf blades; treat stature and habitat as secondary.
5. If fertile material is missing or the awn/ligule characters conflict, retain Sorghastrum sp. pending targeted review.

quick_split: S. nutans — robust tallgrass prairie species with strong collar/ligule cue and dense golden panicle.
S. elliottii — slender eastern/sandy woodland comparison, range HOLD in this project.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: At the grass collar inspect the ligule; then examine mature spikelets and twisted awns. Habitat and panicle color alone cannot identify the species.
shared_traits: Warm-season perennial grasses with narrow blades and panicles of awned spikelets
Awn and spikelet hair details are more reliable than golden panicle color

species_comparison_matrix.character: Lemma awn bend count and length (primary reproductive comparison)
species_comparison_matrix.nutans: Generally once-bent, twisted awn; Iowa grass treatment reports (6–)8–17 mm, while canonical card uses approximately 10–22 mm.
species_comparison_matrix.elliottii: Northeastern Flora treatment describes twice-bent, twisted awn 20–35 mm.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Measure multiple mature intact awns from lemma attachment to tip with a millimeter scale; note overlapping lengths and abnormal/broken awns; verify local material before hard-key use.

species_comparison_matrix.nutans: Usually dense golden-tawny panicle with conspicuous silky-white hairs along branch joints and spikelet stalks.
species_comparison_matrix.elliottii: Usually more open, less hairy panicle with darker spikelets in Northeastern Flora treatment.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Compare same-stage intact panicles and macro views of branch-joint hairs; color alone is unreliable.

species_comparison_matrix.nutans: Short, stout scaly rhizomes usually present, forming loose clumps.
species_comparison_matrix.elliottii: Northeastern Flora describes lacking rhizomes, with fibrous roots.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Expose base carefully only where collection is appropriate; roots and rhizomes are often absent from photos, so do not force a sterile ID.

species_comparison_matrix.nutans: Stiff membranous ligule, typically ~2–7 mm, flanked by prominent pointed auricle-like projections ('rifle sight').
species_comparison_matrix.elliottii: Canonical species review has not locked an exact ligule/auricle contrast; needs a matched specimen-level check.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Macro at sheath-blade junction with 1-mm scale; do not infer absence of projections without inspecting several mature leaves.

species_comparison_matrix.nutans: Often robust 70–220 cm culms with hairy nodes; dimensions vary with site.
species_comparison_matrix.elliottii: Often slender culms, sometimes glabrous; overall height can still be substantial.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Record culm thickness and node pubescence with ruler; stature alone is weak.

species_comparison_matrix.nutans: Tallgrass prairie; canonical target-zone PASS retained unchanged.
species_comparison_matrix.elliottii: Eastern sandy woodland / coastal-plain tendency; canonical learner range UNRESOLVED retained unchanged.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Habitat may support a hypothesis but never replaces mature spikelet evidence or project county proof.

overlap_cautions: Both species are awned grasses; stature, color and habitat are insufficient alone.
S. elliottii remains a canonical learner comparison with existing range HOLD; this lesson does not change that scientific status.
Published S. nutans awn-length ranges differ among floras; use bend count, panicle hairiness and rhizomes together. Do not use a single absolute length threshold.
S. elliottii now has two physically installed provisional photographs, but neither establishes validated ligule/awn characters. Review their exact pixels and licenses before anatomical arrows.
A source photo of S. nutans flowering anthers does not resolve the ligule, awn bend count or S. elliottii comparison.
Retain source-pool status and target-zone native-range labels; this genus lesson makes no new county determination.
local_lookalikes: Andropogon and Anatherum: compare spikelet grouping, raceme architecture, and awn attachment rather than inflorescence color.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: P1 both: matched fertile lemma awn close-ups with 1-mm ruler, attachment point and bend count visible
P1 both: same-scale complete mature panicles plus panicle-joint hair macros
P1 both: paired collar/ligule and pointed auricle-like projections photographed from two angles
P1 both: fertile spikelet, glumes and reduced hairy sterile pedicel at same magnification
P2 both: basal crowns with/without short scaly rhizomes, only from ethically documented material
P2 both: mature culm nodes and leaf-blade width with millimeter scale
P1 S. elliottii: acquire at least one exact-species licensed learner face photo before claiming visual completion

targeted_handoff.request: Verify S. elliottii collar, ligule, glume, fertile spikelet and awn characters against S. nutans before issuing a firm two-way key.
Find matched collar and spikelet macros; preserve existing Joey reference and source licenses.

Compare Sorghastrum elliottii twice-bent 20–35 mm awns, absence of rhizomes and open less-hairy panicle (Northeastern Flora via WFO) against S. nutans once-bent ~8–17 mm awns, short scaly rhizomes and dense silky panicle (Iowa grass treatment); check regional variability before promoting to firm field key.

genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: Find the grass node and leaf collar. Lift the blade to expose the membranous ligule and paired pointed auricle-like projections, then follow a mature panicle branch to one fertile awned spikelet and its neighboring hairy sterile pedicel. Compare awn bends and lengths before trusting panicle color.

shared_structure_examples.plain: The collar is where the leaf blade meets its wrapped stem sheath; the ligule is a little membrane, and two pointed 'ears' can rise beside it.
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Unfold the blade-sheath junction on a mature leaf; photograph both sides at millimeter scale.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: collar and membranous ligule macro, including pointed side projections
shared_structure_examples.why: Recognizes Indiangrass architecture. The conspicuous rifle-sight collar is especially useful for S. nutans, but S. elliottii needs matched verification before using it as a strict species split.

shared_structure_examples.plain: The branched seedhead and its main axis, not a single giant flower.
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: View a complete ripe panicle side-on; compare spacing of branches and visible hairiness.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched mature panicle and panicle-rachis side views
shared_structure_examples.why: S. nutans is often dense and silky; S. elliottii is described as more open and less hairy. Stage and damage can change this impression.

shared_structure_examples.plain: One seed-bearing grass unit with an awn beside a little hairy stalk that does not bear a normal fertile flower.
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: On one mature branch joint, separate the awned spikelet from its adjacent sterile stalk with a hand lens.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: fertile spikelet, glumes and attached sterile pedicel macro
shared_structure_examples.why: Confirms Sorghastrum reproductive architecture; distinguishes it from superficially similar panicles and raceme groups.

shared_structure_examples.plain: A bristle emerging from the tiny floret covering; its twists and knees are measurable.
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Follow the awn from its base on the fertile lemma to the tip; measure the whole awn and count obvious bends.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched intact awns with mm ruler, side-on and base attached
shared_structure_examples.why: Regional floras contrast generally once-bent shorter awns in S. nutans with usually twice-bent longer awns in S. elliottii; require a series of mature intact awns, not one broken example.

confusable_genera.difference: Bluestems commonly organize paired spikelets along conspicuous racemes, sometimes in fingerlike groups or enclosed by spathes. Sorghastrum has a branched panicle with fertile spikelets beside reduced sterile pedicels; inspect one branch joint.
Cultivated and escaped sorghums can also bear branched panicles; inspect spikelet-pair fertility, glumes, rachis disarticulation and growth context rather than the similar name.
Panicles can be similarly narrow or diffuse, but spikelet architecture, lemma/awn configuration and sterile-pedicel pairing separate them under magnification.

comparison_cards.title: Indiangrasses: count the awn knees
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Isolate several mature fertile spikelets, keeping the lemma awn attached; compare the number of bends and total awn length.
comparison_cards.difference: Typical S. nutans: once-bent and usually shorter; S. elliottii: described as twice-bent and longer (20–35 mm) in Northeastern Flora.
comparison_cards.caution: Bent awns may look differently angled when rotated or broken; source treatments vary for S. nutans lengths. Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review should confirm the two-way rule against regional specimens.
photo_roles: macro showing awn attachment to fertile lemma
whole spikelet with adjacent sterile pedicel

comparison_cards.title: Dense silky panicle versus open sparse panicle
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare fully expanded panicles at matched maturity, then zoom in to branch joints for hairs.
comparison_cards.difference: S. nutans often appears dense and silky; S. elliottii generally more open and less hairy.
comparison_cards.caution: Weathering, developmental stage and variable panicle color overlap. Use awns and vegetative details as corroboration.
photo_roles: panicle rachis and joint hair macros

comparison_cards.title: The 'rifle sight' is a collar feature
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Start on Matt Lavin's now-installed REAL S. nutans collar photo: a membrane projects from the sheath between pointed side projections. S. elliottii collar needs a separate source-authenticated same-scale photograph; don't assert it lacks the structure.
comparison_cards.difference: A prominent rifle-sight-like collar is characteristic of S. nutans; S. elliottii collar needs direct verified comparative documentation.
comparison_cards.caution: Source-author and CC BY-SA 2.0 confirmed and physical JPEG checked; exact pixel-arrow placements and direct S. elliottii 1-mm paired collar still pending.
photo_roles: Now-installed real S. nutans membranous collar photo
Matched S. elliottii collar macro with mm scale (MISSING)

comparison_cards.title: Indiangrass versus big bluestem, switchgrass and Johnsongrass
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Collar first: S. nutans has a long notched membranous ligule with pointed rifle-sight sides; big bluestem has a short hairy ligule and turkey-foot seedhead, switchgrass has a triangular dense hair ligule and airy panicle. Indiangrass's paired-position sterile spikelet is absent, leaving a NAKED pedicel; Johnsongrass retains developed pedicelled spikelets.

items.image_role: Second angle of actual Sorghastrum nutans green leaf blade and open sheath at the stem; short projecting pointed ear-like sheath corners and actual pale ligule region are pictured. Do not label these pointed projections as the MEMBRANOUS LIGULE itself.

Louisiana source, not Hays County; no ruler or precise length in this picture.

what_to_teach_crew: Slender Indiangrass source-candidate vs Yellow Indiangrass: Florida Museum 2024 key says S. elliottii commonly TUSSOK without scaly rhizomes, long mostly 25–40 mm TWICE bent awn, ARCHING PANICLE with branches mainly on one side; S. nutans RHIZOMATOUS, mostly 2–15 mm ONCE bent awn, typically more condensed. Two existing S. elliottii source-labelled heads aren't a measured rhizome + awn voucher, so keep scientific hold and do not infer Hays nativity.
